original_test_intent: Install the approved Linux build and complete package set from a physical USB key, reboot into a usable system and verify event logs against the known-event policy.
original_method: A qualified operator verifies/inserts the signed USB, selects it at local/KVM console and completes the interactive destructive install; the agent may collect approved post-boot inventory and logs.
manual_activity: User confirms signed media, exact wipe target and recovery; qualified operator inserts USB, completes console installation and supervises reboot.
required_inputs: Signed/checksummed Linux USB image and exact release/package baseline
Target disk serial/WWN, partition/format/bootloader and wipe policy
Non-target storage/RAID exclusions and backup/recovery image
UEFI/boot, driver, credential, network and repository policy
Qualified operator, local/KVM/OOB access and known-event allowlist
safety_requirements: Verify installer media and stable target identity at the console before format
Disconnect or explicitly protect non-target disks and arrays
Stop on target ambiguity, unexpected partition proposal, installer/package/boot error, power/thermal/BMC fault or recovery loss
Do not automate disk selection, partitioning, credentials or repeated reboot/recovery
agent_execution_scope: Record pre-install hardware/storage/boot baseline and media checksum
Organize operator installer screenshots and decisions
Collect post-boot OS/kernel/package/storage/health and event evidence if access is approved
Do not insert media, operate the installer, enter secrets, wipe disks or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve media, target/wipe/package/boot and recovery plan
Provide qualified operator and own destructive install/recovery
Review reboot/workability and event triage to decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly states no safe SSH command can replace physical USB insertion and the interactive installer.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a qualified operator at local/KVM console; after reboot, collect read-only complete OS/package/storage/health and journal evidence under approved secure access.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: USB boot, Linux all-package install, event review, reboot workability and source 5/30 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind signed media and every installer decision to an exact stable disk identity, then perform a documented post-boot acceptance and event triage.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds destructive target guards, integrity, evidence and recovery without automating the installer.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No automation replaces the physical/interactive installation; post-boot evidence collection may be assisted.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Package repositories and device drivers can change unless exact artifacts and versions are pinned.

project_override_considerations: Project approval must define the exact Linux image, package set, disk layout, known-event allowlist and whether network repositories are permitted; 'all packages' cannot be inferred generically.
expected_evidence: Stable target/all-disk pre/post partition and boot map
Operator USB insertion, boot selection and installer screenshots/logs
Approved package, kernel, driver and network baseline
Successful reboot/KVM workability plus complete journal/dmesg/syslog/BMC/SEL evidence
Known-event triage, non-target preservation, recovery readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define physical USB Linux installation and post-reboot event validation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Signed media, target/wipe policy, operator, console and recovery are execution prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Adds stable destructive-target identity, signed media, non-target protection and auditable event acceptance to an inherently manual install.
independent_technical_reasoning: The irreversible choice is the installer disk/partition screen, where an SSH session cannot prove the physical USB or safely distinguish similarly sized drives. Stable serial/WWN confirmation at the console and independent recovery access are therefore mandatory before formatting, while post-boot success requires both usable console state and unexplained-event triage.
